title: Check a page in several ways
summary: Accessibility testing needs more than one check.
introduction: Accessibility testing needs more than one check. Your task: Check one form using the keyboard and 200% zoom.
learningObjectives: Check one form using the keyboard and 200% zoom.
Explain the example for check a page in several ways

blocks.text: Accessibility testing needs more than one check. Keyboard use, zoom, contrast tools and screen readers each reveal different problems.

Try runnable HTML here with a keyboard as well as a mouse. A screen reader is a tool that reads page information aloud. Test real pages with people and tools; one automated check cannot prove everything works.

blocks.code:
1. Use Tab and Shift+Tab through the page.
2. Activate controls with Enter or Space.
3. Zoom text and page to 200%.
4. Check labels and error messages.
5. Run an automated accessibility check.
6. Try the main task with a screen reader.
blocks.title: Check a page in several ways

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: Tab tests the control order, while Enter and Space test activation.
Zoom and reading-tool checks reveal problems that a static automatic scan may miss.

blocks.text: You get a list of real problems to fix, such as a hidden focus mark or a field with no label.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: A clean automated report does not prove that every task is easy or understandable. Include manual checks.
